record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: For the components of B(n,d,k) produced by the constructions of Teixidor and Mercat, do those two constructions yield the same irreducible component whenever both are defined?

evidence.quote: Question 2.8. Are the components of B(n, d, k) constructed in [Tei91a] and [Mer99b] the same?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth irreducible complex projective curve of genus $g \geq 2$. For integers $n \geq 1$, $d$, and $k \geq 1$, let
$$B(n,d,k) = \{\, [E] \in M(n,d) : h^0(C,E) \geq k \,\},$$
where $M(n,d)$ denotes the moduli space of stable vector bundles of rank $n$ and degree $d$ on $C$. This is the higher-rank Brill–Noether locus.

Two constructions produce irreducible components of $B(n,d,k)$ of the expected Brill–Noether dimension when their respective numerical hypotheses are satisfied:

(i) Teixidor i Bigas's construction, obtained by degeneration to a chain of elliptic curves (or to suitable reducible nodal curves) and smoothing limit linear series of rank $n$ to produce stable bundles $E$ on $C$ with $h^0(E) \geq k$.

(ii) Mercat's construction, which builds bundles $E$ as successive extensions starting from line bundles (or lower-rank bundles) carrying sections, yielding a family of stable bundles in $B(n,d,k)$.

Whenever the numerical conditions defining both constructions are simultaneously satisfied, each yields an irreducible component of $B(n,d,k)$ of the expected dimension.

Question: Under the assumption that both constructions are defined for given $(g, n, d, k)$, do they always produce the same irreducible component of $B(n,d,k)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey of open questions on higher-rank Brill–Noether theory and coherent systems. No subsequent work was located that explicitly identifies or distinguishes the Teixidor and Mercat components of B(n,d,k); related literature studies these components but does not resolve their coincidence.

status_evidence.title: Higher-rank Brill-Noether loci on nodal reducible curves
status_evidence.snippet: Under conditions similar to those of Teixidor i Bigas and of Mercat, the Brill-Noether loci are nonempty and in many cases have a component generically smooth of the expected dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats Teixidor- and Mercat-type components separately without identifying them.
